title: Design System: Outside In Bass Lab

display.purpose: The stated half of a two-voice heading; Inter at up to 8rem, tracking -.08em.

accent.purpose: The set half, Playfair Display italic at the same size, tracking -.05em. Opt-in only: wordmark, one line of a two-voice heading, or an <em> in a title.

label.purpose: The one place tracking goes positive; small caps need it. Engraved control labels on the neck and the fascia use this role.

shadows.name: depth-well
shadows.purpose: A milled well. Depth is a hairline inside the edge, not a cast shadow.

shadows.name: depth-press
shadows.purpose: Pressed or selected surfaces; the edge brightens rather than the surface lifting.

shadows.name: flame-glow
shadows.purpose: The only cast light in the system: a warm glow beneath the flame pill on hover.

shadows.name: lamp-bar
shadows.purpose: The fascia's engaged switch. A lit bar along the top edge keeps the label readable while it is on; a fill would not.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: The one curve. Entrances and state changes share it.

motion.name: m-click
motion.purpose: State change on a control: fill, ink, edge.

motion.name: beat-ms
motion.purpose: While the transport runs, motion is expressed in musical values and route changes land on the next eighth. Stopped, everything falls back to fixed values.

inputGates.name: pointer-coarse
inputGates.purpose: Touch targets are gated on the input device, not the viewport: a propped tablet needs 44px as much as a phone, a mouse at 1200px needs none of it.

components.name: Flame Pill
components.description: The one action on a screen. One per screen, and none when there is nothing to do.

components.name: Ghost Pill
components.description: The default control. Transparent, hairline edge, ink-2 label.

components.name: Floating Nav Pill
components.description: Sections centred in a glass pill that floats clear of the top edge; the page runs underneath it. Hidden below 900px, where the contents control becomes the whole navigation.
components.html: HomePracticeLabs

components.name: Field
components.description: Text entry. Recessed rather than outlined; the flame draws the focus ring and never reshapes the element.
components.html: <input class="ds-field" value="Am9 | D13 | Gmaj9" aria-label="Chord progression">

components.name: Fret Pad
components.description: One fret on the harmony neck. Rank is carried by ink and weight, the wash says where to aim, the ring marks the anchor. Colour is never the only code.

components.name: Deck Switch
components.description: A fascia control. States its function above its value, permanently. Engaged takes a lit bar along the top edge rather than a fill, so the label stays readable while it is on.

components.name: Readout
components.description: The tape counter. The one number read from across the room mid-bar: tabular, large, and the only thing on the panel allowed to be that size. It counts in flame while the transport runs.

components.name: Ladder Rung
components.description: Stepped state reads as a level, not a toolbar. A rung's lamp is the pass colour below the current position, the flame at it, and unlit stock above.

narrative.overview: The instrument photographed, not diagrammed. A dark full-bleed image with the interface floating over it, and a light you move across the picture to reveal what is underneath. The loudest thing on any screen is the photograph; the chrome is glass over the top of it. Three things carry the look and all three are pinned. **Type is two voices in one line**: Playfair Display italic and Inter alternating inside a single heading, the first clause set and the second stated. Tracking is negative everywhere and hard negative on display, which is most of why it reads expensive. **Everything interactive is a pill**, without exception, because a half-measure between pill and square reads as neither. And **colour is almost absent**, one orange spent on the single thing to press, with every other distinction carried by white at four opacities. The restraint is the point. A design with one accent and four greys puts all of its energy into the imagery and the type, which is why it survives being applied to a dense working screen and not just a hero.
keyCharacteristics: Photography is the ground; the interface floats over it in glass.
One orange. If two things on a screen are orange, one is wrong.
Every control is a pill; nothing is square.
Playfair italic is an accent, never a display default.
Tracking is negative everywhere, hardest on the sans display line.
Entrances arrive out of blur, on one exponential curve.

rules.name: The One Flame Rule
rules.body: One orange element per screen, and none when there is no action to take. **One exception, scoped to `.hfString`:** the harmony fretboard carries four hues, because on that board the job a note is doing is the content and not decoration, and four jobs told apart only by opacity are four jobs the player has to stop and decode. See The neck, below. Nothing outside the board may read `--pad-voice`, `--pad-colour` or `--pad-guide`.

rules.name: The Four Greys Rule
rules.body: Every distinction that is not "press this" is carried by white at one of four opacities. Reaching for a fifth colour means the hierarchy has not been thought through.

rules.name: The Photograph Wins
rules.body: Nothing in the chrome may compete with the image. When a surface and a photograph both want attention, the surface loses.

rules.name: The Accent Is Opt-In
rules.body: `--font-display` is Inter. Playfair is reached only through `--font-accent`, and only for the wordmark, one line of a two-voice heading, or an `<em>` inside a title. Pointing the display token at Playfair put every lesson title and the word PASSED in italic serif, which turns an accent into a typeface.

rules.name: The Tracking Rule
rules.body: Negative everywhere: `-.02em` as standard, `-.05em` on the serif display line, `-.08em` on the sans. This is the cheapest thing in the design and the largest part of its character.

rules.name: The Floating Chrome Rule
rules.body: Nav and dock float over the content and never reserve space in the layout. A bar that pushes content down is not this design.

rules.name: Blur Is For Fixed Things
rules.body: If it scrolls, it does not blur.

rules.name: Depth On Black Is A Lit Edge
rules.body: A cast shadow onto `#000` is invisible, so the fascia builds depth from material rather than from shadow. A **plate** is a surface at `--lift`, lit along its top edge and dark along its bottom, and it reads as sitting on the ground: square-edged, because a bolted panel zone has a hard corner. A **well** is darker than the ground it sits in with the light on its inner top edge, and it reads as cut in: milled at `--r-well`, because the things cut into a panel are the rounded ones. A zone is one or the other, never both. Controls sit proud on their plate and move their lit edge to the inside when engaged. Nothing casts onto anything else; the flame's glow is still the only cast light in the system.

rules.name: The Pill Rule
rules.body: Interactive means fully rounded. No exceptions, no partial radii.

rules.name: A Focus Ring Does Not Reshape
rules.body: Never set `border-radius` in a `:focus-visible` rule. The outline already follows the element's shape, and setting a radius there changes the **element**, which with a pill radius drew an orange ellipse around the page heading on every navigation.

rules.name: Rank is ink, and ink is monotone
rules.body: The classifier returns eleven roles; the tutor panel names all eleven and the board shows five steps, because five is what the eye separates at a glance. Every step down is a step dimmer, with no exceptions and no role brighter than a role above it.

rules.name: Highlight is aim
rules.body: Ink says what a note is; the wash says where to go, and it weakens as the reason to play the note weakens. The two ranks that ask for movement are the loudest, because a player looking up mid-bar is looking for the next place to put a finger.

rules.name: Two rings, ranked like the ink
rules.body: Root takes the flame ring; guide takes a hairline; the next chord’s target takes the white ring on `::before`. Approach and outside take none — they are already the dimmest ink and that is the mark. There were five rings on a 52-cell board once, which is the same as none. `::after` belongs to role and `::before` to destination; never let one draw into the other’s pseudo-element.

rules.name: The fret grid is a measurement, not a type step
rules.body: `--hf-nut` and `--hf-fret` are px, and the fret width is set per label mode from the widest label that mode can produce: 84px for the role words, 56px for the two-name accidentals, 44px for note names and targets. The board scrolls rather than shrinking; a neck at half scale is neither playable nor readable. Nothing may leave a fret: the pad clips, and a label that outgrows its fret ends in an ellipsis inside its own cell.

rules.name: The wires are the frets
rules.body: Each pad carries the line on its leading edge at `--rule-strong`, so wires land exactly on the grid columns at any fret width. The first fret in a row has none — the nut is already that line. String rows are separated at `--groove`, a step lighter than the wires, because frets are what you are counting. The string itself runs through the middle of the row behind the notes, so it is never the row’s boundary.

rules.name: One fascia, no pages
rules.body: Everything the session needs is on a single plate, and the deeper material hinges open in place. Reference lives on its own surface at `/practice/manual`; the session surface never navigates.

rules.name: An engraved label per function
rules.body: Every switch states what it does above what it currently says, permanently, in the panel: `30-DAY MAP / 0 of 30`, `THIS DAY / Why`, `BLOCK / Procedure`. The label is `--font-display` at `--t-micro`, uppercase, tracked, `--ink-4`, and it never moves or changes size. This is the correction to a page that had 170 pieces of 11px text doing the work engraving should do.

rules.name: Drawers are shut, and shut costs nothing
rules.body: A drawer that collapses to a header still spends a rule and a line of panel. These are absent until their switch is thrown, and the switch on the bar is what says they exist. Four of them carry what used to be displayed at once: the thirty-day map, why the day exists, the block's five-step procedure, the row generator, the fault log.

rules.name: The lamp, not the fill
rules.body: An engaged switch takes a lit bar along its top edge (`inset 0 2px 0 0 var(--flame)`) over a `--flame-wash` ground, so the label stays readable while it is on. A solid flame fill is reserved for the one thing to press.

rules.name: The flame follows the running process
rules.body: Stopped, the transport's first control is the flame. Running, it has become PAUSE in `--stop` and the flame moves to COMPLETE, while the readout above counts in flame. One lit control at any moment, never two. Both rules read the transport's own state with `:has`, so no new markup can drift out of step with the component.

rules.name: The readout
rules.body: The block timer is the one number read from across the room mid-bar: tabular mono, up to 3.75rem, and the only thing on the panel allowed to be that size.

rules.name: The ladder
rules.body: Stepped state reads as a level, not a toolbar: a rung's lamp is `--pass` below the current position, `--flame` at it, and `--lift-2` above.

rules.name: The list is a list
rules.body: The session's blocks carry an index, a name, a duration and a state lamp. The task and the pass standard belong to the block you have selected and are stated by the panel beside it. A list you scan and a panel you read are different jobs, and giving both jobs to one element is what made this surface unreadable.

**Do** keep one flame element per screen, and none when there is no action.
**Do** carry every other distinction with white at four opacities.
**Do** make every interactive element a fully rounded pill.
**Do** reach for Playfair only through `--font-accent`, and only for a
